newsitem.title: INDIA: Intel says US computer growth reasonable.
newsitem.headline: Intel says US computer growth reasonable.

text.p: Intel Corp president Craig Barrett said on Friday that U.S. computer sales were growing at a reasonable rate, and dismissed industry concerns about a significant slowdown.
"The U.S. market still continues to grow at a reasonable rate," Barrett told a news conference in New Delhi.
He said that over the past 10 years, there had regularly been articles in industry magazines talking of a slowdown which did not take place.

"Each year, there are the same articles forecasting gloom and doom," said Barrett, who was in the Indian capital to promote a drive to boost the use of computers with chips made by his company, the world's largest chip maker.

"What is happening is that the rate of growth has slowed down," Barrett said, adding that it was being offset by high growth in nations like China, Brazil and India, whose markets were growing but with smaller volumes.
Barrett is designated to take over as chief executive officer of Intel after the retirement of Andy Grove.
Barrett said he saw no threat to Intel's multimedia chips using MMX technology from cheaper substitutes made by Advance Micro Devices Inc (AMD), which makes chips with a licence from Intel.

Barrett said he believed Intel's chip technology was flexible enough to account for future changes that would enable it to face competition. "We think we have a highly 'scalable' architecture," he said.
